steps.name: Ela
steps.text: 'We will be connecting with three other nomadic cities. This will be the prelude to the Kazimierz Major...'

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Looks like I picked a bad time to come here.
The ground is damp, as though rain had just fallen.

Ela looks up at the darkened sky, but she could not tell whether the sun was being blocked by dark clouds that had yet to disperse, the towering skyscrapers, or the bright advertising boards on the walls that are lit bright like it was midnight.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: 'Even outside tournament season, our abundant sightseeing and shopping attractions will make your trip more than worth your while.' Let me see...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Visit 'Słoma Food Company HQ'... 'Słomaland'... 'Słoma Prime Mall'... 'Słoma Night Expo'...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And two 15% off Słoma coupons.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Is there no other place that I can go?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Is that it?

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: You should have taken one brochure each from Słoma, Mieszko and Rose Paper Union at the entrance, Miss Ela.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And who might you be?

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: You were previously employed at Dossoles by Reynell Kowalski, whose whereabouts are presently unknown. Where is he now?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I haven't seen him since I left Dossoles.

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: Nevertheless, we would much appreciate your assistance. He left behind a considerable amount of assets in Kazimierz when he disappeared irresponsibly.

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: As someone who has had dealings with him in Dossoles, your statement will help our cause in the division of his assets... and yours.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You mean I'll get a bunch of cash.

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: We will compensate you, commensurate with—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Looks like I really came at a bad time.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Let me make this clear. I haven't seen him and his fox ears since I left Dossoles. I don't want anything to do with his 'business' or 'assets.'
Ela walks away from the man dressed in black and gets on a taxi by the roadside.
In her hurry, she drops the Słoma tourism brochure in a puddle on the ground, dyeing the puddle a bright shade of pink.

steps.name: Unremarkable Man
steps.text: ...Why did you come to Kazimierz, then, if you didn't want to get involved?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Good thing the hotel's not far from the city gates...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Excuse me.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: ...They're still following.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Is that a quiet alley up ahead? Just what I needed.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Can't call it a coincidence anymore.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: (Whisper) First time the modified GRZMOT Mine sees action. No need to thank me.

steps.name: Stalker
steps.text: Come quietly and you won't have to get hurt.

steps.name: Trembling Voice
steps.text: Y-You there! What are you doing?!

steps.name: Stalker
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Tsk!

steps.name: Man in Reporter Garb
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You awake?

steps.name: Man in Reporter Garb
steps.text: I didn't think you would be able to deal with that guy on your own... where did he go?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Ran away. Couldn't go after him with you on the ground like that. What's your name?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Rafał. I'm a reporter. What about you?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Ela.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I've heard that name before... you were Reynell's bodyguard in Dossoles, weren't you?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Guy's more famous than I thought.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Reynell Kowalski always makes great headlines, after all.
Rafał takes out a cigarette and tugs it behind his ear.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Can I ask you a few questions? Before the incident—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Enough questions. Are you able to make it home?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Sorry, I'll be going.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Time to drop by the Rhodes Island office. Here's hoping nothing weird happens from this point on.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Make a right there.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I said, make a right—

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Sorry, I was listening to the tournament results. I made a killing on this one. I'll turn the next corner.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I thought there were no majors going on right now.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Small tournaments happen all the time. There's an arena quite close to here. Would you like to take a look?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Not interested.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Come on, let's go, everyone who comes here goes there—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Take me to the destination that I asked for. There, you missed another turn.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Sorry, sorry—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Don't apologize. Just slow down; the next turn is coming up.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I said, slow down—
Ela tries to open the door, but it is locked tight, and the driver continues to look absent-minded.
Suddenly, she is reminded of Reynell, who landed safely in a pool after jumping from a great height.
This is Kazimierz, not Poland. She is an outsider. Who knows what Originium Arts can do in the hands of these people?
She glances at the driver's right foot, and takes out a gun.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: No sudden moves.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: What the—
Ela reaches out with her foot and stomps on the idle pedal.
The wheels lock and skid, but manage to stop before the intersection.
A large truck rumbles through the intersection that the taxi would have driven through.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Now, I want an explanation—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Hey, where did he go?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Just a driver who got carried away after winning a few coins. He wouldn't have gotten away if anything happened to you.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I have reasons to believe he used Originium Arts or some device to escape. I drove the car over. It's right there. You can examine it.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Really? Where is it?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Right there, in the parking lot—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: It's gone?!

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Lady, I understand you may have been feeling emotional, but you can't just go around accusing people without proof.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I saw it with my own eyes, officer! That truck passed right in front of the nose of the taxi that she was in and almost hit it!

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: And who are you?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: A reporter passing by! There was someone stalking this Miss Ela over here, forcing her to use force—

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Get out.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: This is going in the papers, I tell you!

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: You write whatever you want. Now, get out!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: So you were stalking me too?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I—alright, I'm sorry. You were Reynell's bodyguard, after all. I thought you might have something to offer.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And you were hoping I would be thankful for your 'help' when you saw the car accident?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Wait, Miss Ela. First the stalker, then the accident. Don't you find it suspicious?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I don't need you to tell me.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I have an idea who the culprit is!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Reynell's uncle, Bogdan Kowalski.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: He had been demanding his share of Szczepan's inheritance. With Reynell missing, he probably believed you were here to handle the assets for Reynell, and decided to dispose of you.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Dispose of? Is Kazimierz a place where you can kill people on a whim?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Of course not, but the rich and powerful can always find someone to do their dirty work.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Thank you for the heads-up. It might be helpful.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Are you leaving?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Quite the contrary. I'm not changing my schedule just because of this. Besides, those who treat human lives so callously need to be taught a lesson.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: What are you planning?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Keep looking for clues. There's bound to be something.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: There's one right here. Abetting murder.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: That's not enough.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: It's enough when you have a reporter... I'll be straight with you. Do you want to work with me and teach that old man a lesson?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Did you also work as Reynell's bodyguard?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I'm serious. I have a score or two to settle with old Bogdan.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I was once the chief editor of a newspaper agency under the Rose Paper Union banner. Bogdan hosted an art exhibit five years ago, and it was a complete mess, yet all the media did was lick his boots.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I felt someone had to speak the truth, show the public how bad the exhibit was, so I wrote a column criticizing it overnight...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And it never made it to the printing press?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: It did. It was well-received, and sales of the paper shot up. I thought I was going to get a raise. Here, I kept a copy.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You certainly didn't mince words.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: A month later, I learned that Bogdan had been pressuring the agency to fire me, but the company president stepped in and kept me around as a reporter in the field, where I've been keeping a low profile.
Ela sizes the reporter up as he folds up the yellowish newspaper and tucks it away.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: What are you planning?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Simple. Find concrete evidence that the accident was a murder attempt and seize the initiative.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: (Whisper) Bogdan often talks business here. We might learn something if we eavesdrop.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: (Whisper) Shh, I hear a car.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I know that guy, and I know that car...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I'll pick the lock once the driver has gotten off. Keep watch for me.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I'll—

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Let me do it. I know Kazimierz cars better.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Hey, what's this?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Everything in this alley has been turned upside down. There's no point—

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: A check... with Kowalski's signature?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Looks like we got lucky.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: O-Of course.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I wonder how long it will last.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Well... hehe...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Did you see the one who tried to recruit you when you first arrived?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I'm checking...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Huh? What?

steps.name: Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Dad, I lost again.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I told you not to bet on the tourneys... hey, where did you get the money?

steps.name: Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Lear lent me some.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I'm busy, and I don't have any money.

steps.name: Voice from the Phone
steps.text: But you said you were going to—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: There, he's wearing a suit like yours.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I see him.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Your daughter?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Heh... yeah. She bets on the tourneys every day. If she doesn't get money from me, she tries to borrow it from somewhere else.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Anyway, enough chit-chat. We're the stalkers this time.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Here's what we have so far...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: A photo of an unidentified device, a check found in an alley, and a photo of the man who spoke to me entering Kowalski manor.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I'm not sure how these constitute any sort of his 'weakness.'

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: If that's enough to convict Bogdan, I'll have even less faith in the judicial system of Kazimierz than I do in their law enforcement.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: A draft doesn't necessarily have to be sent out. The same goes for evidence.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Don't you understand?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I'm understanding less and less by the minute.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Sigh.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: We'll send him evidence of him hiring killers as a warning, as well as demand compensation.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: You can use that money to visit the other cities. The cities of the Kawalerielki Alliance are all the same; if you've seen one, you've seen them all.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Me? I'll take the money and ply my trade somewhere else, maybe go home and start a news agency. I want to put the Rose Paper Union out of business in my hometown.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You still want to be a reporter?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Why do you think I became one in the first place? Why else would I pick a fight with Bogdan?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Isn't that blackmail?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: So what? He actually tried to kill you.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Why stop there, then? Why not bring Kowalski down entirely?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: What the heck are you talking about?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You wanted to ask me about Reynell, didn't you? Well, I heard a thing or two about Reynell's parents from a gentleman by the name of Miłosz while I was in Dossoles.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Miłosz... Reynell's secretary?
Rafał's eyes light up, but the spark is soon covered up by his thick lenses.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: See, you're interested.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I... I don't think those two have anything that can deal a real blow to Bagodan, not even if it's from that Miłosz's mouth.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Szczepan and Alizja were a loving couple. Not much of a story there.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Miłosz had a different story.
Rafał's lenses could no longer hide the spark in his eyes. He takes out a pen, then tucks another cigarette behind his ear.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I don't smoke, but this helps me think when I'm working.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Do you know about the damaged statue that was sold for an astronomical price shortly before Alizja passed away? According to Miłosz, there was in fact no deep meaning behind it, as Szczepan had boasted of.
Ela narrated the story as told to her by Miłosz, avoiding subjective sentiments as much as possible.
Before phrases like 'verbal assault' and 'economic control', however, 'loving couple' seems like a bad joke.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Good heavens... what about Reynell? He always looked like he respected his father greatly!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: There is only a twisted hatred for his hypocritical father. Why else would he have blown up his own Galería Krysztauowa?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: He blew it up? That's totally different from the story that's out there! Please, I really must know more! I'll pay—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Where's the money from? The blackmail? Or the money that Bogdan already paid you?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Obviously—

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: (Eyes wide open)

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Miss Ela, this is no time for jokes! I'm not—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Drop the act, Mr. Rafał.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Everything that has happened up to this point, the chance encounter, the shadowing, evidence that just dropped from the sky... they're suspicious, but it wasn't out of the question that they could have been a coincidence.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You want to blackmail Bogdan Kowalski.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: A few words from him were enough to ruin your career, and yet you wanted me to blackmail him, in a place where both the police and the courts could be bought.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Don't lie to me. I'm not Kazimierzian. You are.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Why attempt something that's almost destined to fail?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Because you wanted me to come under suspicion of blackmail, and get the police and the courts on Bogdan's side.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I didn't have a choice... you heard the phone call... I needed money...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Why should I believe you?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: (Heavy breathing) I swear, I may have sold my dignity to Bogdan, but every word I said about my career was true.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And the newspaper? You didn't throw it away as soon as the curtains closed, did you?
After a moment of silence, Rafał takes out the yellowish newspaper cutting, folded as neatly as the last time Ela saw it.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I never threw it away.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Then it's your turn to fight back.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Fight back? The story about Szczepan and Alizja is a good one, but what does it have to do with Bogdan?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: If Alizja's statue was made under coercion, violence and lies, what about the other artworks that Bogdan has?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: *Kazimierzian profanity*!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Let me make this clear: This will shake the very foundation of the art market of Kazimierz. Reynell wanted to do it. It was a roundabout method that almost killed a bunch of people, but in the end, he failed.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Why didn't he let the world know? I doubt it's to protect the father he hated.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I know, Miss Ela. I know. Kazimierz won't allow it.
He takes out a lighter, hand fumbling as he fetches the cigarette from behind his ear, lights it, and takes it in deeply. His face is deathly pale.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I thought I could keep it there. Sorry. But I must say, Miss Ela...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I may not be the first reporter in Kazimierz to know about it, maybe not even the first who's tried to bring it to light...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: But I stand on the same side of the curtain as the shocking truth. Maybe hundreds of people have stood here before, and no one even found their bodies...

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Chrzanić to! I'm tearing this curtain in half!

steps.name: Humble Secretary
steps.text: Bogdan Kowalski foolishly threatened your life and safety. You acted reasonably in self-defense.

steps.name: Humble Secretary
steps.text: Plus, Rhodes Island is an important guest of Kazimierz... the Chamber has nothing to say about Bogdan. What he wants will never belong to him.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Humble Secretary
steps.text: Now, I ask that you honor our gentleman's agreement.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Could I go back on it even if I wanted to?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You people had everyone concerned in custody two hours before the feature on the Kowalski family hit the press, and made the paper come up with a replacement article within the hour.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I learned a lot from Kazimierz today.

steps.name: Humble Secretary
steps.text: As we did from you. Less than a month into your visit to Kazimierz, you stirred up a storm that almost destroyed an entire industry.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: (Shrugs) One last request. Can I see Rafał? Where is he?

steps.name: Humble Secretary
steps.text: He is doing well. We can approve your request for a visit if you insist, but we will require further... conditions in our agreement.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Ela. You doing ok?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I've been given preferential treatment thanks to some unexpected ties... is this the new job that the General Chamber of Commerce got you? What do you do now?
Rafał's lip twitches as he glances at his collar, where there seems to be a metallic glint of sorts. He lights a cigarette for himself.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: I'm, *cough*, reviewing newspapers prior to publication.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Sorry, I always prefer to have it behind my ear, but I needed something to calm my nerves.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Is it such a bad thing to get a first-hand look at the process and standards?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Terrible. Look at what I have to review every day.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: 'The Red Wine'?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: A good paper, isn't it?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Looks like whoever made this decision had a twisted sense of humor.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Let's talk about something else. How's your daughter? Is your new income enough to support her gambling?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: (Wry smile) Enough to get the best seats. She's one of their best customers now.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: ...It really does sound terrible.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: It is, but everything is getting better.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: And what does that mean?

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: It means Kazimierz never changes. I'm the only one who does.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: They're willing to pay me a lot of money. All I need to do is... behave.
Rafał inhales deeply and gazes at the ceiling. This time, Ela can see the microphone underneath his collar clearly.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: You see that? High-tech stuff, here to help me behave, just like the salary that I wouldn't even have dreamed of just a few days ago.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Not a gadget I dare to get rid of. As for the other... soon, I wouldn't want to be rid of it.

steps.name: Rafał
steps.text: Dreams and willpower can be worn down. When it's all said and done, everything will get better, and I'll be a model Kazimierz citizen, just like my daughter.
Rafał puts the cigarette out and goes back to his place in a long row of office seats.
Ela scans the room. All of them seem to be doing the same work as Rafał. Some look frustrated, some look numb, and some look around uneasily...
How many of them have said, 'chrzanić to'? Maybe it was just Rafał, who is now winking at her, or maybe it was all of them.
Ela gives Rafał an encouraging gaze, and glances down at the issue of The Red Wine in her hand.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Zofia

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Zofia?!

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: 'Whislash' Zofia. Now that's an exciting coincidence.

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: Excuse me, am I speaking to Miss Ela?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: I'm the manager of the Gale Knightclub. We would like to inquire into your interest in participating in knight tournaments...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: What's next? You want me to pay a registration fee?

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: Perhaps you misunderstood—oh, you want to talk to our patron yourself? Alright, here you go...

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: Miss Ela, I'm the main sponsor of the Gale Knightclub, and a business rival of Bogdan Kowalski.

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: We would like to congratulate you on your good fortune, and we could not help but notice your outstanding skills and judgment in the face of danger—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Maybe we would have gotten along better if you just said you were shadowing me.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: It's the tournaments this time, isn't it?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: The knight tournaments of the country of knights... round one was a draw, Kazimierz. Let's see about round two.
